01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 817

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 817
Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ. Meccan, and it is said Medinan. Its verses: 4. «Revealed after al-Nās.» In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة الإخلاص مكية، وقيل مدنية، وآياتها 4 «نزلت بعد الناس» بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 112:1–4 · Vol. 4, pp. 817–819

Verses 1 to 4

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «Say: He is God, the One (1). God, the Eternal Refuge (2). He neither begets nor is born (3). And there is none comparable to Him (4)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (1) اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ (2) لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ (3) وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ (4)
Vol. 4, p. 817
.» «Huwa» (He) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and «God is One» is the matter itself, as in your saying «He — Zayd is departing»: as if it were said, «The matter is this: that God is one, with no second.»
هُوَ ضمير الشأن، واللَّهُ أَحَدٌ هو الشأن، كقولك: هو زيد منطلق، كأنه قيل: الشأن هذا، وهو أنّ الله واحد لا ثانى له.
Question
If you ask: what is the grammatical position of «huwa»?
فإن قلت: ما محل هو؟
Answer
I say: nominative as the subject, and the predicate is the sentence.
قلت: الرفع على الابتداء والخبر الجملة.
Question
If you ask: a sentence that serves as a predicate must contain a pronoun referring back to the subject; where is the referent?
فإن قلت: فالجملة الواقعة خبرا لا بد فيها من راجع إلى المبتدإ، فأين الراجع؟
Answer
I say: the status of this sentence is that of a single word, as in «Zayd is your servant», in that it is the subject in meaning. That is because the saying «God is One» is the very matter that «huwa» denotes, which is not the case with «Zayd — his father is departing», since Zayd and the sentence denote two different meanings, so something is needed to connect them. From Ibn ʿAbbās: Quraysh said: «O Muhammad, describe to us your Lord to whom you call us,» so it was revealed — that is: He whom you asked me to describe is God. And «aḥad» (One) is a substitution for «God»; or it is on the basis of «He is one»; and it has the sense of «wāḥid», its root being «waḥad». ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ubayy read: «Huwa Llāhu aḥad» without «Say», and in the reading of the Prophet ﷺ: «Allāhu aḥad» without «Say: He is». And he said, of one who
قلت: حكم هذه الجملة حكم المفرد في قولك «زيد غلامك» في أنه هو المبتدأ في المعنى، وذلك أن قوله اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ هو الشأن الذي هو عبارة عنه، وليس كذلك «زيد أبوه منطلق» فإنّ زيدا والجملة يدلان على معنيين مختلفين، فلا بد مما يصل بينهما. وعن ابن عباس: قالت قريش: يا محمد، صف لنا ربك الذي تدعونا إليه، فنزلت: يعنى: الذي سألتمونى وصفه هو الله، وأحد: بدل من قوله، الله. أو على: هو أحد، وهو بمعنى واحد، وأصله وحد. وقرأ عبد الله وأبىّ: هو الله أحد، بغير قُلْ وفي قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: الله أحد، بغير قُلْ هُوَ وقال من
Vol. 4, p. 818
recites «Allāhu aḥad», that it is equivalent to the Qur'ān. Al-Aʿmash read: «Say: He is God, the Single (al-wāḥid).» It was also read «aḥadu Llāh» without tanwīn: it was dropped because of its meeting the definite article lām; similarly: «and not remembering God except little.» [1] The better reading is with tanwīn, and its kasrah is due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. «Al-ṣamad» is of the pattern fiʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, from «ṣamada ilayhi» meaning «he sought him out»; it is the master to whom one turns in needs. The meaning: He is God whom you know and acknowledge to be the Creator of the heavens and the earth and your Creator; He is one, unique in divinity, with none sharing in it; and He is the one to whom every creature turns, having no independence from Him, while He is self-sufficient with regard to them. «He neither begets» — because He has no kind (is not of a genus), such that He would have a consort of His kind and they would reproduce; and He indicated this meaning in His words «How could He have a child when He has no consort?» «Nor is He born» — because everything born is originated and a body, whereas He is eternal with no beginning to His existence, and is not a body. «And none is comparable to Him» — that is, none is equal to Him or resembles Him; it may also derive from «kafāʾah» in marriage (equality of match), denying a consort. They asked Him to describe Himself to them, so there was revealed to him what comprises His attributes: His words «He is God» point them to the One who is the Creator and Originator of things, and within that is a description of Him as powerful and knowing, because creation requires power and knowledge, being based on utmost perfection, harmony and order; and within that is a description of Him as living, hearing and seeing. His word «aḥad» describes Him with oneness and denies partners. His word «al-ṣamad» describes Him as one who is only turned to, and if He is only turned to then He is self-sufficient; and in His being self-sufficient together with being knowing: that He is just, not doing evil deeds [2], because of His knowledge of the ugliness of what is ugly and His knowledge of His independence from it. His words «nor is He born» describe Him with eternity and priority. His words «He neither begets» deny similarity and homogeneity. And His words «And there is none comparable to Him» confirm that and conclude the judgement upon it. If you ask: it is the eloquent Arabic practice to put the circumstantial phrase that is «idle» (laghw, not a true predicate) after, not before, and Sībawayh stated this in his book [3]; so why is it placed first in the most eloquent and most precise speech? I say: this speech is only aimed at denying equivalence to the essence of the Creator, glory be to Him; and the focus and pivot of this meaning is this
قرأ: الله أحد، كان بعدل القرآن. وقرأ الأعمش: قل هو الله الواحد. وقرئ: أحد الله، بغير تنوين: أسقط لملاقاته لام التعريف. ونحوه ولا ذاكر الله إلّا قليلا «1» والجيد هو التنوين، وكسره لالتقاء الساكنين. والصَّمَدُ فعل بمعنى مفعول، من صمد إليه إذا قصده، وهو السيد المصمود إليه في الحوائج. والمعنى: هو الله الذي تعرفونه وتقرّون بأنه خالق السماوات والأرض وخالقكم، وهو واحد متوحد بالإلهية لا يشارك فيها، وهو الذي يصمد إليه كل مخلوق لا يستغنون عنه، وهو الغنى عنهم لَمْ يَلِدْ لأنه لا يجانس، حتى تكون له من جنسه صاحبة فيتوالدا. وقد دل على هذا المعنى بقوله أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ صاحِبَةٌ. وَلَمْ يُولَدْ لأنّ كل مولود محدث وجسم، وهو قديم لا أوّل لوجوده وليس يجسم ولم يكافئه أحد، أى: لم يماثله ولم يشاكله. ويجوز أن يكون من الكفاءة في النكاح، نفيا للصاحبة: سألوه أن يصفه لهم، فأوحى إليه ما يحتوى على صفاته، فقوله هُوَ اللَّهُ إشارة لهم إلى من هو خالق الأشياء وفاطرها، وفي طىّ ذلك وصفه بأنه قادر عالم، لأن الخلق يستدعى القدرة والعلم، لكونه واقعا على غاية إحكام واتساق وانتظام. وفي ذلك وصفه بأنه حى سميع بصير. وقوله أَحَدٌ وصف بالوحدانية ونفى الشركاء. وقوله الصَّمَدُ وصف بأنه ليس إلا محتاجا إليه، وإذا لم يكن إلا محتاجا إليه: فهو غنى. وفي كونه غنيا مع كونه عالما: أنه عدل غير فاعل للقبائح «2» ، لعلمه بقبح القبيح وعلمه بغناه عنه. وقوله لَمْ يُولَدْ وصف بالقدم والأوّلية. وقوله لَمْ يَلِدْ نفى للشبه والمجانسة. وقوله وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ تقرير لذلك وبت للحكم به: فإن قلت: الكلام العربي الفصيح أن يؤخر الظرف الذي هو لغو غير مستقر ولا يقدم، وقد نص سيبويه على ذلك في كتابه «3» ، فما باله مقدّما في أفصح كلام وأعربه؟ قلت هذا الكلام إنما سيق لنفى المكافأة عن ذات الباري سبحانه، وهذا المعنى مصبه ومركزه هو هذا
Vol. 4, p. 819
phrase; so it was therefore the most important and relevant thing, and the most deserving and apt to come first. «Kufuʾan» was also read with ḍammah on the kāf and the fāʾ, and with ḍammah or kasrah on the kāf with sukūn on the fāʾ.
الظرف، فكان لذلك أهم شيء وأعناه، وأحقه بالتقدم وأحراه. وقرئ: كفؤا، بضم الكاف والفاء. وبضم الكاف وكسرها مع سكون الفاء:
Question
If you ask: why is this sūrah equal to the whole Qur'ān, despite the brevity of its text and the closeness of its two ends?
فإن قلت. لم كانت هذه السورة عدل القرآن كله على قصر متنها وتقارب طرفيها؟
Answer
I say: «for some reason a person becomes a master»; and it is only because it contains the attributes of God Most High, His justice and His oneness. It suffices as evidence for one who acknowledges its merit and believes the words of the Messenger of God ﷺ about it: that the knowledge of divine unity (tawḥīd) has a certain standing with God Most High. How could it not, when knowledge follows what is known: it is honoured by its honour and lowered by its lowliness; and what is known in this knowledge is God Most High and His attributes, what is permissible for Him and what is not? So what do you think of the nobility of its rank and the majesty of its station, its loftiness above every other knowledge and its taking of the lead in the race beyond it? And whoever despises it does so out of the weakness of his knowledge of what is known, the paucity of his veneration of it, his emptiness of fear of Him, and his distance from considering the outcome. O God, gather us among those who know You, who act for You, who affirm Your justice and Your oneness, who fear Your threat. It is also called Sūrat al-Asās (the Foundation) because it contains the fundamentals of the religion. Ubayy and Anas related from the Prophet ﷺ: «The seven heavens and seven earths were founded on “Say: He is God, the One”» — meaning they were created only to be proofs of God's oneness and knowledge of His attributes which this sūrah expresses. It is related from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he heard a man reciting «Say: He is God, the One», and said: «It is obligatory.» He was asked: «O Messenger of God, what is obligatory?» He said: «Paradise is obligatory for him.» [2]
قلت: لأمر ما يسود من يسود، وما ذاك إلا لاحتوائها على صفات الله تعالى وعدله وتوحيده، وكفى دليلا من اعترف بفضلها وصدق بقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها: إنّ علم التوحيد من الله تعالى بمكان، وكيف لا يكون كذلك والعلم تابع للمعلوم: يشرف بشرفه، ويتضع بضعه، ومعلوم هذا العلم هو الله تعالى وصفاته، وما يجوز عليه وما لا يجوز، فما ظنك بشرف منزلته وجلالة محله، وإنافته على كل علم، واستيلائه على قصب السبق دونه، ومن ازدراه فلضعف علمه بمعلومه، وقلة تعظيمه له، وخلوه من خشيته، وبعده من النظر لعاقبته. اللهم احشرنا في زمرة العالمين بك العاملين لك، القائلين بعدلك وتوحيدك، الخائفين من وعيدك. وتسمى سورة الأساس لاشتمالها على أصول الدين. وروى أبىّ وأنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أسست السماوات السبع والأرضون السبع على قل هو الله أحد» «1» يعنى ما خلقت إلا لتكون دلائل على توحيد الله ومعرفة صفاته التي نطقت بها هذه السورة. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سمع رجلا يقرأ قل هو الله أحد فقال: «وجبت» . قيل: يا رسول الله وما وجبت؟ قال: «وجبت له الجنة» «2»
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 818
1. The explanation of this verse of poetry was given in Part One, page 448; refer to it if you wish. End of the corrector's note.
2. His words «that He is just, not doing evil deeds» — this is the doctrine of the Muʿtazilah. The people of the Sunnah hold that He, Exalted, is the Creator of all things, their good and their evil, their ugly and their beautiful. God Most High said: «God is the Creator of all things», and His knowledge of the ugliness of what is ugly does not prevent Him from creating it, since it is for a wisdom, even if no one else knows it. (ʿ = the editor)
3. Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: «If you ask: the eloquent Arabic practice is to put the circumstantial phrase after, and Sībawayh stated this.» Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: Sībawayh reported that he heard one of the coarse Arabs reciting: «wa-lam yakun aḥadan kufuwan lah.» And this boor followed his habit, his coarse nature being unable to grasp the subtlety of the meaning for which the phrase was required to be placed, along with the predicate, before the subject. That is, the purpose for which the verse was sent down is denial of equality and equivalence to the essence of God Most High; so putting first the equivalence — which is intended to be denied of Him — is more fitting. Then, when it was put first in order to be denied, the circumstantial phrase was mentioned with it, in order to clarify the sacred Essence through the denial of equivalence. And God knows best.
1. (1) . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الأول صفحة 448 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
2. . قوله «إنه عدل غير فاعل للقبائح» هذا مذهب المعتزلة، وذهب أهل السنة إلى أنه تعالى هو الخالق لجميع الأشياء خيرها وشرها قبيحها وحسنها. قال تعالى: اللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وعلمه بقبح القبيح لا يمنعه من خلقه، لأنه لحكمة وإن لم يعلمها غيره. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «إن قلت الكلام العربي الفصيح أن يؤخر الظرف وقد نص سيبويه على ذلك» قال أحمد: نقل سيبويه أنه سمع بعض الجفاة من العرب يقرأ: ولم يكن أحدا كفوا له، وجرى هذا الجلف على عادته فجفا طبعه عن لطف المعنى الذي لأجله اقتضى تقديم الظرف مع الخبر على الاسم، وذلك أن الغرض الذي سيقت له الآية نفى المكافأة والمساواة عن ذات الله تعالى، فكان تقديم المكافأة المقصود بأن يسلب عنه أولى، ثم لما قدمت لتسلب ذكر معها الظرف ليبين الذات المقدسة بسلب المكافأة، والله أعلم.
Vol. 4, p. 819
1. I did not find it as a raised (marfūʿ) ḥadīth; Ibn Abī Shaybah related it in Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghaylān al-Thaqafī from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, as a halted (mawqūf) report.
2. Related by al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and al-Ḥākim from the ḥadīth of ʿUbayd ibn Ḥunayn from Abū Hurayrah. It has a corroborating report in al-Ṭabarānī's al-Kabīr from the ḥadīth of Abū Umāmah.
1. (1) . لم أجده مرفوعا «وأخرجه ابن أبى شيبة في فضائل القرآن من رواية عبد الله بن غيلان الثقفي عن العب الأحبار موقوفا.
2. . أخرجه الترمذي والنسائي والحاكم من حديث عبيد بن حنين عن أبى هريرة. وله شاهد في الطبراني الكبير من حديث أبى أمامة.
